findings.title: Horizontal shrink persists a width-2 cell with no continuation into scrollback
findings.evidence: init(6,3) + 'abc界\r\n' + 5 rows + resize(4,2). Scrollback offset 4 reads `61:1 62:1 63:1 754c:2` — a width-2 cell in the final column with nothing after it. The renderer emits .term-wide at two cell widths there and overflows the row. Permanent: it is in history. Separately, the same shrink on the active row deletes the glyph outright (`61:1 62:1 63:1 20:1`) while ghostty keeps a spacer.

findings.title: DECAWM off demotes a wide glyph to width 1 at the right margin
findings.source: found independently by the gate operator and the reviewer
findings.evidence: init(5,2) + ESC[?7l + 'abcd界' → cell(0,4) is `754c:1`. With room it is `754c:2` plus a `0` continuation. The DOM paints a fullwidth glyph in a one-cell span, which is the exact disagreement #54 exists to remove. ghostty drops the glyph instead.

findings.title: unicode_width classifies unassigned and narrow codepoints as wide
findings.evidence: U+3040 (unassigned) reads `3040:2` on the built-in core and `3040:1` on ghostty. A false width 2 makes the renderer emit .term-wide for a narrow character, which is the same misalignment in the opposite direction. The classifier ranges whole blocks rather than following EAW.

findings.title: DCH on a continuation column shifts the row by two columns
findings.evidence: 'A界BC' then ESC[1;3H ESC[1P. Built-in gives `41:1 42:1 43:1 20:1 ...`: the wide glyph is gone and content moved two columns for a one-column delete. ghostty gives `41:1 20:1 42:1 43:1 ...`, one column. ICH shows the mirror: it rewinds the cursor to the wide lead and inserts before the requested column.

findings.title: Ghostty spacer heads are treated as continuations and dropped from the DOM
findings.evidence: wasm_api.zig cellWidth maps both .spacer_tail and .spacer_head to 0. A spacer head at the right margin has no wide cell before it and still owns a column. Renderer row [1,2,3,4,head] renders textContent '1234', expected '1234 '. Cosmetic while the cell is blank; a row background would lose its last column.

exemptions.claim: packages/@wterm/ghostty/README.md left untouched while ghostty/src changed
exemptions.evidence: Read it. It documents install, options and architecture, and defers the cell contract to the TerminalCore interface. The cell shape is documented in packages/@wterm/core/README.md and apps/docs/src/app/api-reference/page.mdx, both in the diff.

exemptions.claim: markdown README and docs page mention width and are not in the diff
exemptions.evidence: Read both. `width` there is MarkdownRenderer's line width in columns, unrelated to cell width.

exemptions.claim: Combining marks and ZWJ sequences consume columns on the built-in core
exemptions.evidence: 'A'+U+0301+'B' leaves cursor.col 3 on the built-in core and 2 on ghostty; the family ZWJ emoji leaves 8 vs 6. printChar advanced one column per codepoint before this PR too, so the behavior is unchanged rather than regressed. unicode_width never returns 0.
exemptions.verdict: pre-existing scope gap, issue candidate below

issue_candidates.title: unicode_width has no zero-width class, so combining marks and ZWJ shift the grid
issue_candidates.evidence: See exemption above. Every codepoint consumes at least one column, so accented text and ZWJ emoji desync exactly the way #54 describes for wide characters.
issue_candidates.scope: pre-existing, adjacent to this PR's premise

issue_candidates.title: The two cores disagree on width for the same input
issue_candidates.evidence: Beyond the findings: U+3040 2 vs 1, combining marks 1 vs absorbed, DCH shift 2 vs 1, right-margin trailing cell 1 vs 0. Two advertised interchangeable cores are observably incompatible on wide-character edges.
issue_candidates.scope: cross-cutting, needs a shared conformance corpus
